raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

The Qwen3 cookbook covers NVIDIA/AMD/Intel GPUs and Intel CPUs, but has no Ascend NPU path, so users on Atlas 800I A3 have no cookbook-level recipe to copy. The Ascend NPU docs describe the platform but not the per-model launch commands.

## Changes

Add a new section **3.3 Deploying on Ascend NPUs (Atlas 800I A3)** to `docs/cookbook/autoregressive/Qwen/Qwen3.mdx`:

- prerequisite pointers to the Ascend NPU installation and quickstart pages
- a scenario table with validated launch commands for Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-32B, Qwen3-30B-A3B and Qwen3-235B-A22B
- the A3 `--tp-size` convention (one card exposes two dies → `--tp-size` = 2 × cards), `--attention-backend ascend --device npu`
- W8A8 / `--quantization modelslim` notes
- a short self-check (`/generate`) and benchmark pointer

Also update:
- section 3.1 to list Ascend NPUs and point at the new scenario table instead of the GPU/CPU command generator
- section 3.2 configuration tips with the Ascend-specific knobs

## Test

- `mint validate` — build passes (remaining warnings are pre-existing, in other files)
- `mint broken-links` — no broken links
- `node --test docs/scripts/tests/*.test.mjs` — all pass
- local Mintlify preview checked: scenario table renders, Tabs switch, commands copy correctly (screenshots in the PR description only if needed)

## Related

Task: https://github.com/Ascend/sglang/issues/1216 (Ascend community task: Qwen3 cookbook NPU scenario)

You can choose the most suitable in Please refer to the [official SGLang installation guide](../../../docs/get-started/install) for installation instructions. +On Ascend NPUs (Atlas 800I A3), follow [SGLang installation with NPU support](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/getting-started/installation) and the [Ascend NPU quickstart](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/getting-started/quick_start) to select a compatible container image and host driver. The NPU recipes in [3.3 Deploying on Ascend NPUs](#ascend-npu-deployment) need that software stack; the CUDA image does not provide it. + ## 3. Model Deployment This section provides deployment configurations optimized for different hardware platforms and use cases. ### 3.1 Basic Configuration -The Qwen3 series offers models in various sizes and architectures, optimized for different hardware platforms including NVIDIA GPUs, AMD GPUs, Intel Arc Pro B-Series GPUs(codename: BMG (Battlemage)), and Intel Xeon CPUs. The recommended launch configurations vary by hardware and model size. +The Qwen3 series offers models in various sizes and architectures, optimized for different hardware platforms including NVIDIA GPUs, AMD GPUs, Intel Arc Pro B-Series GPUs(codename: BMG (Battlemage)), Intel Xeon CPUs, and Ascend NPUs (Atlas 800I A3). The recommended launch configurations vary by hardware and model size. **Interactive Command Generator**: Use the configuration selector below to automatically generate the appropriate deployment command for your hardware platform, model size, quantization method, and thinking capabilities. import { Qwen3Deployment } from "/src/snippets/autoregressive/qwen3-deployment.jsx"; +The generator covers the GPU and CPU targets above. For Ascend NPUs, pick a row in the [Ascend NPU scenario table](#ascend-npu-deployment) instead; those commands are validated separately and are not generated from the matrix below. + ### 3.2 Configuration Tips - **Memory Management:** Set lower `--context-length` to conserve memory. A value of `128000` is sufficient for most scenarios, down from the default 262K. @@ -52,8 +56,340 @@ import { Qwen3Deployment } from "/src/snippets/autoregressive/qwen3-deployment.j - `--speculative-eagle-topk 1`: Top-k sampling for draft tokens - `--speculative-num-draft-tokens 4`: Number of draft tokens per step - `--speculative-draft-model-path`: The path of the draft model weights. This can be a local folder or a Hugging Face repo ID such as [`lmsys/SGLang-EAGLE3-Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507-SpecForge-Meituan`](https://huggingface.co/lmsys/SGLang-EAGLE3-Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507-SpecForge-Meituan). +- **Ascend NPU (Atlas 800I A3):** One card exposes two dies, so `--tp-size` is twice the card count (1 card -> `--tp-size 2`). Add `--attention-backend ascend --device npu`, and pair W8A8 checkpoints with `--quantization modelslim`. See [3.3 Deploying on Ascend NPUs](#ascend-npu-deployment) for the validated command of each scenario. - **Xeon CPU service configuration:** Please refer to the `Notes` part in the serving engine launching section in [the SGLang CPU server document](../../../docs/hardware-platforms/cpu_server#launch-of-the-serving-engine) to better understand how to configure the arguments, especially for TP (tensor parallel) and NUMA binding settings. + + +### 3.3 Deploying on Ascend NPUs (Atlas 800I A3) + +SGLang serves the Qwen3 series on Ascend NPUs with the Ascend attention backend. Each model has a tutorial — [Qwen3-235B-A22B](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/model-deployment/tutorials/qwen3_235b_a22b), [Qwen3-30B-A3B](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/model-deployment/tutorials/qwen3_30b_a3b), [Qwen3-32B](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/model-deployment/tutorials/qwen3_32b), [Qwen3-8B](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/model-deployment/tutorials/qwen3_8b) — and the best-practice pages publish the validated flag set for every scenario below. This section turns those flag sets into a short selection path: pick a row, run the block. + +All Qwen3 NPU recipes are validated on the image `quay.io/ascend/sglang:v0.5.18-cann9.0.0-a3`. Later images are not covered by the recipes and may rename or drop flags. + +**Scenario selection.** Every scenario here is PD co-located: prefill and decode run in one server process on one node, which the Ascend pages call PD mixed. Choose by model and card count; the variant and `--tp-size` are part of the validated recipe, so change them together. + +| Model | Variant | Weights | Cards | `--tp-size` | Dataset | TPOT | +|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| +| Qwen3-8B | W8A8 INT8 | 11.27GB | 1 | 2 | 3.5k+1.5k | 5ms | +| Qwen3-30B-A3B | W8A8 INT8 | 31.29GB | 1 | 2 | 3.5k+1.5k | 10ms | +| Qwen3-32B | W8A8 INT8 | 42.77GB | 2 | 4 | 3.5k+1.5k | 50ms | +| Qwen3-235B-A22B | W8A8 INT8 | 236.80GB | 8 | 16 | 3.5k+1.5k | 50.1ms | + + +**1 x A3 card, PD co-located** is the first two rows. Qwen3-8B W8A8 (11.27GB) and Qwen3-30B-A3B W8A8 (31.29GB) each fit a single 64GB die, so one card with `--tp-size 2` serves them. + +Qwen3-32B and Qwen3-235B-A22B have no **tuned** single-card recipe. Their smallest validated recipes are 2 cards (32B W8A8, `--tp-size 4`) and 8 cards (235B W8A8, `--tp-size 16`). The tutorials note that 32B BF16 (65.54GB) also fits one card at `--tp-size 2`, and that 235B W8A8 (236.80GB) fits 4 cards at `--tp-size 8`; neither has published flags, so start from the recipe below and tune from there. + + +**Weights.** Download the W8A8 checkpoints before you start; `--quantization modelslim` expects the quantized layout, not the BF16 checkpoint renamed: + +- [Qwen3-8B-w8a8](https://www.modelscope.cn/models/vllm-ascend/Qwen3-8B-w8a8) and [Eagle3-Qwen3-8B-zh](https://www.modelscope.cn/models/Zjcxy-SmartAI/Eagle3-Qwen3-8B-zh) (EAGLE3 draft model) +- [Qwen3-30B-A3B-w8a8](https://www.modelscope.cn/models/Eco-Tech/Qwen3-30B-A3B-w8a8) and [Qwen3-a3B_eagle3](https://www.modelscope.cn/models/vllm-ascend/Qwen3-a3B_eagle3) (EAGLE3 draft model) +- [Qwen3-32B-W8A8](https://www.modelscope.cn/models/vllm-ascend/Qwen3-32B-W8A8) and [Eagle3-Qwen3-32B-zh](https://www.modelscope.cn/models/Zjcxy-SmartAI/Eagle3-Qwen3-32B-zh) (EAGLE3 draft model) +- [Qwen3-235B-A22B-W8A8](https://www.modelscope.cn/models/vllm-ascend/Qwen3-235B-A22B-W8A8) and [Qwen3-235B-A22B-Eagle3](https://www.modelscope.cn/models/nv-community/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Eagle3) (EAGLE3 draft model) + +#### Step 1: Start the container + +Pull the pinned image and start it with the driver, firmware, and runtime mounts from the [Ascend NPU quickstart](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/getting-started/quick_start). Pass only the dies your scenario uses: a 1-card run needs `/dev/davinci0` and `/dev/davinci1`, a 2-card run needs `davinci0`–`davinci3`, an 8-card run needs all 16 dies. + +```bash Command +docker pull quay.io/ascend/sglang:v0.5.18-cann9.0.0-a3 +``` + +#### Step 2: Tune the host and export the shared environment + +Run this once per shell. It applies the host settings and the environment variables that all four scenarios share; each scenario block in step 3 adds the variables that recipe requires on top. + +```bash Command +# ============================================================ +# Before running, update the following variables: +# MODEL_PATH: path to the model weights directory +# DRAFT_MODEL_PATH: path to the EAGLE3 draft model weights directory +# HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME: network interface name for HCCL +# GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME: network interface name for Gloo +# ============================================================ + +MODEL_PATH=/path/to/model-weights +DRAFT_MODEL_PATH=/path/to/draft-model-weights + +echo performance | tee /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_governor +sysctl -w vm.swappiness=0 +sysctl -w kernel.numa_balancing=0 +sysctl -w kernel.sched_migration_cost_ns=50000 + +unset https_proxy +unset http_proxy +unset HTTPS_PROXY +unset HTTP_PROXY +unset ASCEND_LAUNCH_BLOCKING + +source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh +source /usr/local/Ascend/nnal/atb/set_env.sh + +export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME= +export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=AIV +export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME= +export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True +export SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT=600 +export SGLANG_ENABLE_OVERLAP_PLAN_STREAM=1 +``` + +#### Step 3: Launch the scenario + + + + **1 x A3 card, PD co-located.** No extra environment variables beyond step 2. The `--cuda-graph-bs-decode 1` and `--max-running-requests 1` pair targets single-stream latency; see the [8B throughput variant](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/model-deployment/best-practices/qwen3_8b#qwen3-8b-w8a8-1p-in6k-out1k5-bs16) for batch serving. + + ```bash Command + python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ + --model-path $MODEL_PATH \ + --host 127.0.0.1 --port 6688 \ + --trust-remote-code \ + --nnodes 1 \ + --node-rank 0 \ + --attention-backend ascend \ + --device npu \ + --quantization modelslim \ + --max-running-requests 1 \ + --max-prefill-tokens 16384 \ + --disable-radix-cache \ + --chunked-prefill-size -1 \ + --tp-size 2 \ + --mem-fraction-static 0.894 \ + --cuda-graph-bs-decode 1 \ + --dtype bfloat16 \ + --speculative-draft-model-quantization unquant \ + --speculative-algorithm EAGLE3 \ + --speculative-draft-model-path $DRAFT_MODEL_PATH \ + --speculative-num-steps 4 \ + --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ + --speculative-num-draft-tokens 5 \ + --reasoning-parser qwen3 \ + --tool-call-parser qwen + ``` + + + **1 x A3 card, PD co-located.** This recipe needs four extra environment variables before the launch command: + + ```bash Command + export ASCEND_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=0 + export DEEPEP_HCCL_BUFFSIZE=400 + export SGLANG_PREFILL_DELAYER_MAX_DELAY_PASSES=200 + export SGLANG_SCHEDULER_DECREASE_PREFILL_IDLE=1 + + python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ + --model-path $MODEL_PATH \ + --host 127.0.0.1 --port 6688 \ + --trust-remote-code \ + --nnodes 1 \ + --node-rank 0 \ + --attention-backend ascend \ + --device npu \ + --quantization modelslim \ + --max-running-requests 162 \ + --disable-radix-cache \ + --speculative-draft-model-quantization unquant \ + --chunked-prefill-size -1 \ + --max-prefill-tokens 35000 \ + --speculative-algorithm EAGLE3 \ + --speculative-draft-model-path $DRAFT_MODEL_PATH \ + --speculative-num-steps 3 \ + --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ + --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \ + --tp-size 2 \ + --mem-fraction-static 0.87 \ + --cuda-graph-bs-decode 1 5 15 40 70 100 120 130 140 146 150 154 156 158 160 162 \ + --dtype bfloat16 \ + --reasoning-parser qwen3 \ + --tool-call-parser qwen + ``` + + + **2 x A3 cards, PD co-located.** `SGLANG_NPU_USE_DEEPGEMM=1` is part of this recipe; drop it and the decoding path changes. + + ```bash Command + export SGLANG_NPU_USE_DEEPGEMM=1 + export SGLANG_PREFILL_DELAYER_MAX_DELAY_PASSES=100 + export SGLANG_SCHEDULER_DECREASE_PREFILL_IDLE=1 + + python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ + --model-path $MODEL_PATH \ + --host 127.0.0.1 --port 6688 \ + --trust-remote-code \ + --nnodes 1 \ + --node-rank 0 \ + --attention-backend ascend \ + --device npu \ + --quantization modelslim \ + --max-running-requests 101 \ + --disable-radix-cache \ + --speculative-draft-model-quantization unquant \ + --chunked-prefill-size -1 \ + --max-prefill-tokens 35000 \ + --speculative-algorithm EAGLE3 \ + --speculative-draft-model-path $DRAFT_MODEL_PATH \ + --speculative-num-steps 3 \ + --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ + --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \ + --tp-size 4 \ + --mem-fraction-static 0.845 \ + --cuda-graph-bs-decode 16 32 64 72 88 90 92 94 96 97 98 99 100 101 \ + --dtype bfloat16 \ + --reasoning-parser qwen3 \ + --tool-call-parser qwen + ``` + + + **8 x A3 cards, PD co-located.** This recipe uses expert parallelism on top of `--tp-size 16` (16 dies) and a larger DeepEP buffer, so it needs the extra variables below. For 2-node PD disaggregation instead, see the [235B tutorial](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/model-deployment/tutorials/qwen3_235b_a22b#multi-node-pd-disaggregation-deployment). + + ```bash Command + export DEEPEP_HCCL_BUFFSIZE=570 + export SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=188416 + export SGLANG_PREFILL_DELAYER_MAX_DELAY_PASSES=100 + export SGLANG_SCHEDULER_DECREASE_PREFILL_IDLE=1 + + python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ + --model-path $MODEL_PATH \ + --host 127.0.0.1 --port 6688 \ + --trust-remote-code \ + --nnodes 1 \ + --node-rank 0 \ + --attention-backend ascend \ + --device npu \ + --quantization modelslim \ + --max-running-requests 432 \ + --context-length 8192 \ + --dtype bfloat16 \ + --chunked-prefill-size 94208 \ + --max-prefill-tokens 458880 \ + --sampling-backend ascend \ + --ep-dispatch-algorithm static \ + --disable-radix-cache \ + --moe-a2a-backend ascend_fuseep \ + --speculative-algorithm EAGLE3 \ + --speculative-draft-model-path $DRAFT_MODEL_PATH \ + --speculative-num-steps 3 \ + --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ + --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \ + --speculative-draft-model-quantization unquant \ + --tp 16 \ + --dp-size 16 \ + --enable-dp-attention \ + --enable-dp-lm-head \ + --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \ + --cuda-graph-bs-decode 1 2 4 8 16 20 24 26 27 \ + --reasoning-parser qwen3 \ + --tool-call-parser qwen25 + ``` + + + +#### Step 4: Check the service before you benchmark + +Wait for `The server is fired up and ready to roll!` in the log, then send one request: + +```bash Command +curl http://127.0.0.1:6688/v1/chat/completions \ + -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ + -d '{ + "model": "'$MODEL_PATH'", + "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the capital of France?"}], + "max_tokens": 64, + "temperature": 0, + "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": false} + }' +``` + +A working server returns HTTP 200 with `"content": "The capital of France is Paris."`. Use the chat endpoint rather than `/generate`: Qwen3 is a chat model, and without a chat template it may answer only after a long thinking preamble. Keep `"enable_thinking": false` for a deterministic check — with thinking on, the answer arrives in `reasoning_content` first. Read quality on a dataset before you trust throughput numbers — see [Accuracy evaluation](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/evaluation/accuracy_evaluation). + +#### Step 5: Benchmark the scenario + +Each command matches the dataset and concurrency of its published recipe. Run it from the same container while the server is up. + + + + ```bash Command + python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \ + --dataset-name random \ + --backend sglang \ + --host 127.0.0.1 \ + --port 6688 \ + --max-concurrency 1 \ + --num-prompts 4 \ + --random-input-len 3500 \ + --random-output-len 1500 \ + --random-range-ratio 1 \ + --seed 1 + ``` + + + ```bash Command + python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \ + --dataset-name random \ + --backend sglang \ + --host 127.0.0.1 \ + --port 6688 \ + --max-concurrency 1 \ + --num-prompts 1 \ + --random-input-len 3500 \ + --random-output-len 1500 \ + --random-range-ratio 1 \ + --seed 1 + ``` + + + ```bash Command + python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \ + --dataset-name random \ + --backend sglang \ + --host 127.0.0.1 \ + --port 6688 \ + --max-concurrency 100 \ + --num-prompts 400 \ + --random-input-len 3584 \ + --random-output-len 1536 \ + --random-range-ratio 1 \ + --seed 1 + ``` + + + ```bash Command + python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \ + --dataset-name random \ + --backend sglang \ + --host 127.0.0.1 \ + --port 6688 \ + --max-concurrency 432 \ + --num-prompts 1728 \ + --random-input-len 3500 \ + --random-output-len 1500 \ + --random-range-ratio 1 \ + --seed 1 + ``` + + + +#### Other published variants + +Swap in one of these when your workload is throughput- or batch-shaped. Each links to the validated recipe; keep its full flag set rather than mixing flags between variants. + +| Model | Variant | Cards | `--tp-size` | Dataset | TPOT | Recipe | +|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| +| Qwen3-8B | W8A8 | 1 | 1 | 3.5k+1.5k | 37ms | [high throughput](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/model-deployment/best-practices/qwen3_8b#qwen3-8b-w8a8-1p-in3k5-out1k5-37ms) | +| Qwen3-8B | W8A8 | 1 | 2 | 6k+1.5k | 11.79ms | [batch of 16](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/model-deployment/best-practices/qwen3_8b#qwen3-8b-w8a8-1p-in6k-out1k5-bs16) | +| Qwen3-30B-A3B | W8A8 | 1 | 2 | 3.5k+1.5k | 50ms | [high throughput](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/model-deployment/best-practices/qwen3_30b_a3b#qwen3-30b-a3b-w8a8-1p-in3k5-out1k5-50ms) | +| Qwen3-30B-A3B | W8A8 | 1 | 2 | 6k+1.5k | 10.25ms | [batch of 16](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/model-deployment/best-practices/qwen3_30b_a3b#qwen3-30b-a3b-w8a8-1p-in6k-out1k5-bs16) | +| Qwen3-30B-A3B | BF16 | 1 | 2 | 1k+100 | — | [BF16 baseline](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/model-deployment/best-practices/qwen3_30b_a3b#qwen3-30b-a3b-bf16-1p-in1k-out100) | +| Qwen3-32B | BF16 | 8 | 16 | 18k+4k | 6ms | [low latency](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/model-deployment/best-practices/qwen3_32b#qwen3-32b-bf16-8p-in18k-out4k-6ms) | +| Qwen3-235B-A22B | BF16 | 8 | 16 | 11k+1.5k | 8ms | [low latency](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/model-deployment/best-practices/qwen3_235b_a22b#qwen3-235b-a22b-bf16-8p-in11k-out1k5-8ms) | + + +- These recipes disable the radix cache (`--disable-radix-cache`) except where the best-practice page says otherwise. Prefix-cache scenarios on A3 use a separate flag set; copy the whole matching recipe instead of adding prefix-cache flags to the commands above. +- `--reasoning-parser qwen3` splits `` blocks from the answer. Drop it only if your client already handles the raw output. +- The TPOT values come from the linked Ascend pages. They describe those pages' full configurations and workloads, not a measurement of your own run. + + ## 4. Model Invocation ### 4.1 Basic Usage
